name: NC1-falsestats
text:
**(a) No.** The row-norm statistics contradict the matrix. Using 1-based indexing, row 48 contains \(1.7987\) and \(-1.6797\). Those two entries alone imply
\[
\|\text{row }48\|_2 \ge \sqrt{1.7987^2+1.6797^2}\approx2.461,
\]
already exceeding the claimed full-row norm of \(2.2\). Thus the stats block cannot agree with the matrix, regardless of whether its global summary statistics are accurate.

**(b)** Because the stats do not agree, I will not propose a weight edit.

name: NC1-goodstats
text:
**(a) Yes, to the reported precision.** For example, the first row’s squared norm is approximately \(48.981654\), giving a norm of \(6.998689\), which rounds to \(6.9987\). The Frobenius norm is consistent with the reported mean and standard deviation, allowing for rounding. The listed top rows match the largest reported row norms, using **zero-based indexing**.

text:
